headline: Notice issued on challenge to automated blocking
body: On 19 November, a Delhi High Court Bench of Acting Chief Justice Nitin Wasudeo Sambre and Justice Sanjay Sharma issued notice to the Union of India and Meta on LiveLaw's petition challenging Rule 4(4) of the IT Rules, 2021, which requires large platforms to use automated tools to restrict content exactly identical to content already removed.

LiveLaw says three Instagram reels reporting Supreme Court hearings were restricted in India, two within about 15 minutes of posting, without any order, notice or reasons. The Additional Solicitor General suggested treating the petition as a representation and passing a reasoned order; LiveLaw's counsel called that a mere formality.
The Union and Meta have four weeks to file replies. Interim relief was not pressed. The matter is listed next on 18 January 2027, and similar challenges on 9 February 2027.

headline: Hearing adjourned to 9 December
body: On 17 November, the Supreme Court listed the challenge to the DPDP Act's amendment of the RTI Act together with the connected petitions, including the Digital News Publishers Association's. The matter could not be taken up and was adjourned to 9 December.
On 27 October, the Court had issued notice on the news publishers' petition and declined an interim stay without hearing the Union. The RTI petitions were referred to a larger bench in February 2026.

headline: Six URLs to be taken down in interim order
body: On 6 November, the Delhi High Court directed that six URLs carrying the AI-generated videos and images complained of be taken down, in an interim order in Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta's suit against the Aam Aadmi Party.
The Court issued summons. The defendants are yet to be heard. The suit is listed next on 4 December.

headline: High Court suspends Collector's order said to rely on AI
body: On 3 November, Justice N.V. Shravan Kumar of the Telangana High Court suspended the Jangaon Collector's order of 8 September in a land dispute. The petitioner says the order was passed ex parte, with AI tools and without verifying the facts.

The Court issued notice to the Revenue Principal Secretary, the Collector and the Tahsildar, and asked the Advocate-General what action is proposed. The matter was listed on 18 November; the outcome has not been reported yet.

headline: Banks must compensate victims where due diligence fails
body: On 29 October, a Bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana said the RBI's proposed anti-cyber-fraud regulations must require financial institutions to compensate victims where a fraud results from a failure of due diligence. The compensation must be at least equal to the customer's loss.
The Court said it would examine the draft regulations before they are notified. The RBI proposed notifying them by 30 November and bringing them into operation by 31 December.

The Court directed WhatsApp and other intermediaries to set out the measures they propose to prevent digital arrest scams, and to share them at the same time with the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C). Counsel for WhatsApp said the platform had acted against about 9,400 accounts.

The RBI was directed to file a list of all authorised financial institutions, and law enforcement agencies to report the status of digital arrest FIRs. The order was uploaded on 7 November, and the case was listed next on 23 November.

headline: Summons issued; no interim relief yet
body: On 16 October, Justice Tejas Karia of the Delhi High Court issued summons in Kent RO Systems' suit against Amazon over the use of KENT as a sponsored-ads keyword, and on Kent's application for an ad interim injunction. Amazon accepted notice.
No interim relief has been granted. Amazon's reply to the application is due within three weeks and its written statement within 30 days. The application is listed next on 8 December.
